extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, IP Australia staff, and IP practitioners who rely on IPA examination practice guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for patent examination and related procedures at IP Australia, covering search and classification, formalities, examination standards (novelty, inventive step, sufficiency), amendments, oppositions, hearings, register matters, and international/PCT practice. Intended to direct examiner practice and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and expectations for the quality of examination and other work outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes quality requirements, peer review, and criteria used to assess the quality of reports and decisions (see also Annexes and specific quality checklists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Service Charter (Timeliness Guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness and customer service standards to be observed in dealings with applicants and third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets guidelines on response times and timeliness expectations for reports and other communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practices to ensure efficient conduct of patent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers use of Earlier Search and Examination Reports (FERs), general approach to examination, level of detail in reports, reserving opinion, restricting the search, and communicating with applicants/third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FERs (Earlier Search and Examination Reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how to make use of earlier search and examination reports in current examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for leveraging existing reports to avoid duplication and to inform the examiner's search/analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of Detail in the Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on appropriate detail to include in first and subsequent examination reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies expectations for the amount and granularity of reasoning, evidence citations, and conclusions in reports; adjustments for second and later reports are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserving Opinion and Restricting the Search
rubrics_metrics.description: When examiners may reserve a firm opinion or restrict the extent of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains circumstances where reserving opinion or restricting search scope is appropriate, and how to communicate such reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating with the Applicant and Third Parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for contact, correspondence and disclosure to applicants and third parties during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes permitted and prohibited communications, informal communications, and procedures for third party observations/notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assisting Unrepresented Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on assisting applicants who are not legally represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets boundaries for assistance, ensures fairness, and avoids giving legal advice or compromising impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Delegations, and Restrictions on Providing Customer Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing delegations of authority and restrictions on advice/examination assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Commissioner’s power to make delegations, conflict of interest rules, what advice may be provided to applicants/third parties, and other restrictions on examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: The theoretical basis for conducting patent prior-art searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers objectives of the search, iterative searching, and how theory informs practical search strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of the Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals that a patent search must achieve (e.g., identify relevant prior art for novelty/inventive step assessments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides selection of areas to search and level of comprehensiveness required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The expectation that searching is an iterative process refined as understanding of the invention develops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on revisiting searches as claim construction and search results evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Classification Systems (IPC, CPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and structure of patent classification systems (International Patent Classification, Cooperative Patent Classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains IPC/CPC structure, headings/titles, definitions, notes/warnings, function/application-oriented places, references, indexing codes, combination sets and revisions; how to find and use classification symbols when searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and priority rules for allocating classification places to a document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes invention information vs additional information, application of indexing codes/2000 series, classification priority rules (common, first-place, last-place, special rules), classifying combinations and chemical compounds, C-set allocation and syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Search Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-search tasks e.g., identifying inventive concept, considering earlier search results, and deciding on additional/top-up searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes approaches to construction and inventive concept identification, reviewing earlier search results, preliminary search steps, applicant/inventor name searching, and criteria for top-up searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of the Search Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: How to design a search strategy tailored to the claims and invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers use of a Three Person Team (3PT) for searching, considerations for independent/dependent/broad claims, reserving the search, use of controlled language, and selection of search areas (patent literature, classification, non-patent literature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting the Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical conduct of searches and analysis of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes techniques for conducting searches, analyzing and culling documents, when to cease searching, and categorising and recording relevant citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording the Search Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for recording what was searched and search outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes completing Search Information Statements, documenting fields searched, dates, documents considered relevant, family member identification, and date of actual completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Information Statement (SIS) Completion
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how to complete the Search Information Statement for sequence and chemical structure searches and other cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex examples and instructions for completing SIS and when it must be completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three Person Team (3PT) Use in Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Role and procedures for a three-person team in search activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines responsibilities, contribution to search allocation and quality, and annex guidance on the 3PT role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary and Top-Up Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: When preliminary or additional (top-up) searches are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides deciding extent of search needed (including use in international/PCT contexts) and how to cost/allocate top-up searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification-Based Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: How and when to use classification symbols to find prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains finding classification symbols, using them in searches, and special practices such as Japanese FI/F-Term classification and C-sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Patent Literature Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations and methods for searching non-patent literature (NPL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies when NPL is relevant and best practices for locating and citing NPL sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and Categorising Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to categorise and cite prior-art documents in reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on citation categories, selecting documents considered relevant, citing URLs, family members, and relating citations to relevant claim numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Procedures — Re-Examination and Section 104 Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and criteria for re-examination and for amendments under section 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conditions to commence re-examination, process, completion, requirements for section 104 amendments, who can request amendments and timing, and requirements to provide reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Legislation and Working with Case Law/Statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interpreting legislation and applying case law and statutory provisions in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guide to interpreting legislation and integrating precedent and statutory interpretation into examiner decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities and Forms — Formalities Checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements to be checked at filing and during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists formalities required at filing (e.g., credible address for service), formalities during examination, and how to process substitute pages and returns/deletions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Requirements of the Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting and content requirements for the specification (title, abstract, text, pagination, formulas, drawings, sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies requirements for abstracts, titles, text formatting, equations, drawings, graphics, photographs, amino acid/nucleotide sequences, and handling scandalous matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved Forms and Signature Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for using approved forms (including patent request) and signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General and specific requirements for approved forms and signature/authentication requirements for filed documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement (Who Can File/Be Granted a Patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for entitlement to file and to be granted a patent, including statements of entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples of declarations, treatment of artificial intelligence inventorship and legal person examples and organisations of uncertain legal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Specifications, Claims and Claim Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose and principles of construing the specification and claims for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers initial considerations, addressee, role of common general knowledge, rules of construction (plain meaning, read as whole, purposive construction, dictionary principle, reject absurd, technical document approach), and treatment of errors/omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Construction for a Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules to apply when construing specification text for meaning and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains giving words plain meaning, reading specification as a whole, purposive construction, dictionary principle, rejecting absurd interpretations, treating the description as technical, and dealing with errors/mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction and Claim Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach to construing claims and considerations for different claim types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes that claims are legal documents, presumption against redundancy, omnibus claims, Swiss claims, product-by-process, parametric claims, 'for use' wording, open/closed claim language ('comprises/includes/consists of'), reference numerals, relative terms, qualifiers like 'substantially/about/generally', appended claims and claim drafting issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination — Relevant Dates, Definitions and Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Key dates (priority, filing, publication) and legal standards applied in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines priority and filing dates, effect of publication, definitions of invention/alleged invention/document meaning, and use of the balance of probabilities standard in factual assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to Consider Before Commencing Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and procedural checks before starting substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers request for examination, state of lapse, extensions of time, payment of fees, translations and translation verification, obtaining priority documents, excess claims fees and invitations to pay, and report dispatch/corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and Claims to Examine
rubrics_metrics.description: Which documents and versions to examine and how to treat amendments made prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing consideration of amendments, unity (single invention), omnibus claims, provisional specifications, and guidance on claim sets to be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations: Prior Art Base and Construction of Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: What counts as prior art, how to construe cited documents, and the level of disclosure required to object under prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes public availability, exclusions, grace period, whole-of-contents objections, enabling disclosure, clear/unmistakable directions, single source versus combination of documents, and third party notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and practice for assessing novelty, whole-of-contents objections, secret use and selections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on determining novelty with specific examples, issues for chemical compositions, prior use and confidential information, and how selections affect novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements, tests and information to assess inventive step (non-obviousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out statutory basis, tests for inventive step, factors and indicators to assess inventive step, information to consider, and special issues for chemical compositions and other fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Disclosure, Sufficiency, Clarity and Support (Section 40 considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for clear and complete disclosure and support for claims under s40 (sufficiency/best method/support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes that claims must be clear and succinct, s40(2)(a) clear and complete disclosure, s40(3) support for claims, difference between disclosure and support, best method requirement, deposit of micro-organisms, claims defining the invention, and examples of subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Define the Invention / Claims are Clear and Succinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that claims define the invention and must be clear and succinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on drafting and evaluating clarity and succinctness of claim language and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Method / Full Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to disclose the best method known to the applicant for performing the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers date for determining full description, ascertainability of nature of invention, enabling disclosures, effort required to perform, and aspects claimed across different claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Eligible Subject Matter (Manner of Manufacture, Usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for assessing whether subject matter is patent eligible (manner of manufacture / usefulness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses general principles, alleged inventions, fine arts, discoveries/ideas/theories/schemes/plans, printed matter, computer-implemented inventions, games, mathematical algorithms, methods of testing/measurement, mere working directions, nucleic acids and genetic info, micro-organisms, treatment of human beings, agriculture, combinations/kits, new uses, utility, and historical annexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance, Grant and Refusal of Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions, timing and grounds for acceptance, postponement, extension or refusal of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conditions/time for acceptance, postponement/extension/cancellation, revocation of acceptance, refusal circumstances, continued examination processes, lapsing and withdrawal, double patenting issues, parallel applications, registration and QRS issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to claim divisional status, priority entitlement, time limits, and examination of divisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conditions for when a divisional can be filed, relation to the parent, procedural outlines for divisional examination and annex guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents of Addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions and examination practice for patents of addition (improvements/modifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers conditions for filing, differentiation from the parent, examination of addition applications and amendment of the parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Search and Opinion (PSO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for requesting and responding to preliminary search and opinion requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes PSO request procedure, search/examination procedure for PSO, report requirements and response handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes and grounds to commence and complete re-examination of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out commencement procedures, re-examination steps, completion, and outcomes including refusal or revocation following re-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition Orders (Defence and Associated Technology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling applications subject to prohibition orders for defence/associated technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects of prohibition orders, special handling of applications concerning defence of the Commonwealth and associated technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Patents (system and examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance for innovation patents including formalities, examination, determining innovative step, certification, opposition and expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers types of innovation patents, formalities check, examination practice, criteria for innovative step, certification/opposition processes and relevant annex forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments — What Can Be Amended and When
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope and timing for amendments to filed documents and specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains which documents can be amended, who may request amendments (including consent requirements), when amendments may be requested, requirements to provide reasons, withdrawal of amendments, circumstances preventing processing, fees, and guidelines for completing allowance forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Allowability of Proposed Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Required form and tests for allowability of proposed amendments to complete specifications (before/after acceptance/grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes format requirements (statement of proposed amendments), allowability tests at different stages (prior to acceptance, after acceptance, after grant), non-allowable amendments, amendments after grant, and opposition to amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Correct Clerical Error or Obvious Mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and evidence needed to correct clerical errors and obvious mistakes in filed documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines clerical error and obvious mistake, and outlines evidence required for correction requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments Relating to Micro-Organisms and Sequence Listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for inserting/altering sec 6(c) information and correcting sequence listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for handling sequence listing amendments and related deposit/biological material requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments During Opposition Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: How amendments are processed, considered and potentially opposed during opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers initial processing of amendment requests, considering amendments and opponent comments, amendments as result of hearing decision, appeals and checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions — Procedural Summaries and Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules for opposing grants of standard patents, innovation patents, extensions of term, section 104 amendments, time extensions, licences and other opposition types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on commencing oppositions, filing statements of grounds and particulars, evidence periods, finalising oppositions and special forms for different opposition types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directions in Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanics and grounds for directions given in opposition or entitlement proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes directions to stay proceedings, requests for further particulars, filing times for evidence, general conduct and further directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence — Presentation and Admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for presentation, admissibility and timing of evidence in opposition/hearing proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers written evidence and affidavits, oral evidence, physical evidence special considerations, admissibility rules and late-filed evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of Documents and Summonsing Witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Power and basis for summonsing witnesses and requiring production of documents or articles in proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines statutory bases for issuing summonses, production requests, reasonable expenses, compliance excuses, sanctions for non-compliance and schedule requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and Dismissal of Oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for withdrawing or dismissing oppositions and related consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes withdrawal processes for different opposition types, dismissal requests, dismissal on Commissioner initiative, reasons for dismissal and handling of withdrawal of opposed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings and Decisions — Setting Down Hearings and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: How hearings are scheduled and conducted, decision-making standards and publication/timeframes for decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers setting hearings, locations/options for appearance, hearing hours, fees, who may appear, interactions with court actions, ex parte hearings, natural justice rules and bias, principles of conduct (lawfulness, fairness, rationality, openness, diligence, courtesy, integrity), written decisions, time for issuing decisions, publication, rectification of errors, revocation and quality requirements including peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Conduct for Hearing Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected professional conduct standards for hearing officers and hearing officer appointment/standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes appointment/delegations, hearing officer panels, assistant officers, and standards panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs — Principles in Awarding Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and scales for awarding costs in proceedings and grounds for exemplary awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers scale of costs, variation, awarding and taxation of costs, security for costs and exemplary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Register of Patents — Recording and Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: What the patent register is, how particulars are recorded and amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recording new particulars, change of ownership (assignment, change of name, bankruptcy, winding up, death), security interests, licences, court orders, equitable interests, effect of registration/non-registration, trusts, false entries, and procedures for rectification and error amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Time and Restoration of Priority (Section 223)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules, grounds and procedure for requesting extensions of time and restoration of priority rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers section 223 grounds (office error, error or omission, circumstances beyond control, despite due care), filing requests, Commissioner discretion, common deficiencies in requests, advertising extensions, interplay with acceptance, payment of fees and related procedural points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Time under Regulation 5.9
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and criteria for extensions of time under Reg 5.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to request an extension, legal application of the regulation, justification, discretionary matters, period granted, hearings and reviews, out-of-time evidence and parties involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of Right of Priority under the PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedure for restoring PCT priority rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps to apply for restoration and documentation required under PCT rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Term for Pharmaceutical Substances (Section 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules for extensions of patent term for pharmaceutical substances, including definition and application procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers meaning of 'pharmaceutical substance', 'mixture or compound' meanings, 'in substance disclosed', first regulatory approval date, applying and processing an extension, documentation, timing, calculating extension length, opposition to extension, and related case law references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders for Inspection of non-OPI Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for inspection of documents that are not open public information (non-OPI) by Commissioner direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for documents not OPI, inspection processes and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals (ART, ADJR, Courts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paths and procedures for appealing decisions to Federal Court, Administrative Review Tribunal, judicial review (ADJR) and other courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes processes for appeals, section 105 amendments and interplay with court actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computerised Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority and processes related to making, substituting and managing computerised decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines power to make computerised decisions, substitution, and management of existing computerised decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superseded Legislation and Practice — Summary and Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of earlier legislation/practice and guidance on transitional approaches in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarises relevant legislative changes, general approach to examination under superseded law, and differences in law/practice; includes discussion of amendments, novelty, inventive/innovative step practice and section 40 practice under older law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Step / Innovative Step Indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance specific to assessing 'innovative step' (innovation patents) including indicators and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists indicators of inventive/innovative step, examples, and how to apply them in examination of innovation patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 40 Specifications (Historical/Specific Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance on section 40 requirements including what is the invention, full description, claims as fair basis, and sub-tests for fair basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses approach in leading cases (e.g., Lockwood v Doric), consistory clause, essential features, critical analysis requirement, best method, enabling disclosures, relation between described invention and claimed invention, alternatives, claiming by results, reach-through claims, claims to alloys and more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Dates and Filing Dates Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed treatment of priority date determinations for claims and related complications (convention applications, amended claims, associated applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on determining priority dates for claims, for convention applications, relation to amended claims and priority documents that are provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified and National Phase Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for modified examination regimes and national phase applications under PCT/national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers national phase preliminaries, formality requirements, priority sources, whether PCT Article 19/34 amendments are considered, and examination practice for national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention and PCT Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and guidance for convention applications and all PCT-related searching and examination steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes PCT procedural outlines for international search and examination, unity of invention, claim interpretation under PCT guidelines, search strategy, ISR/ISO/IPER/notification form completion, subjects excluded from search, claim interpretation hierarchy and other PCT considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Searching and International Examination Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for acting as an ISA/IPEA or RO in PCT international search and examination contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers extent of search, minimum documentation, allocation of searches, unity of invention, search strategies, abstracts/titles, excluded subjects, claim interpretation, top-up searches, written opinions, IPRPII, completing forms and annex quality checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO, Other Countries and Foreign Search Aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for handling WIPO searches, other national practices, and use of foreign patent search aids/documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes WIPO request guidelines, completion times/priority, search procedures, assistance with foreign languages, obtaining full text and hard-copy documentation, and background search aids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous International/PCT Administrative Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative allocations, roles, staffing and capabilities related to international/PCT duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes current allocation of PCT duties, international online specialists, authorised officers, minimum levels of responsibility, examiners with foreign language capabilities and APO status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexes and Checklists (ISR Quality Checklist, IPE Quality Checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental annexes and completed-form examples to guide completion and quality control (ISRs, ISOs, annex examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex materials include blank/completed ISRs, examples of inventive step objections, PCT forms, internet searching guidance, best practice examples and quality checklists to ensure consistent reporting.
